anya: Heads-up — trying to bring up an HF model 'faux-llm/special-chat' for eval. It requires trust_remote_code and a custom architecture. redwood convert keeps choking on tokenizer placeholders and chat templates. Anyone hit this before?

sam: Can you paste the convert error / minimal logs?

anya: Sure — short excerpt:
```
$ redwood convert-hf faux-llm/special-chat --out ./models/special-chat
INFO: fetching config/tokenizer
INFO: detected custom modules -> requires trust_remote_code
ERROR: Conversion failed: Unsupported custom class: 'CustomChatModel' (auto_map missing)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "redwood/convert.py", line 312, in convert
    model = load_model(cfg)
  File "redwood/loader.py", line 78, in load_model
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported custom class: '{cls_name}'")
ValueError: Unsupported custom class: 'CustomChatModel'
```

anya: Also the tokenizer ended up with weird special tokens; conversation templates replaced user placeholders with literal tokens like '<|user|>' in the prompt that HF expects as a tag, but our runtime treats differently.

priya: Two common paths: 1) vendorize the model's remote code (copy the custom classes into our models repo) and run conversion with trust_remote_code disabled; 2) allow trust_remote_code during conversion and add a safe whitelist so loader can instantiate the class. Both have tradeoffs.

mike: For quick unblock I usually vendorize. Also check tokenizer.json for 'special_tokens_map' and 'added_tokens'. If the HF tokenizer relies on custom special_tokens_map names (e.g., 'pad_token_id' vs 'pad_token') we mis-map during conversion.

anya: Here's the tokenizer snippet I found in the repo: 
```
{
  "special_tokens_map": {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "user_token": "<|user|>", "assistant_token": "<|assistant|>"},
  "added_tokens": [{"id": 50256, "content": "<|user|>"}, {"id": 50257, "content": "<|assistant|>"}]
}
```

sam: Ah, custom names 'user_token' / 'assistant_token' are not standard keys transformers expects. Our redwood converter maps known keys (bos, eos, pad, unk). So those two silently fell through and became "added_tokens" only — later the chat template uses {user} placeholder that converter replaced with the literal token text causing double-escaping.

priya: Workaround steps I recommend: 
1) vendorize the HF repo into our models/ directory (git subtree or copy)
2) patch config.json to include an auto_map entry: 
```
"auto_map": {"AutoModelForCausalLM": "custom_module.CustomChatModel"}
```
3) update tokenizer.json to standard keys: map 'user_token' -> 'additional_special_tokens' and ensure 'special_tokens_map' uses 'bos_token'/'eos_token'.
4) run redwood convert with `--trust-remote-code` disabled after vendorizing (loader will import local module).

mike: Also watch out for quantization: after conversion we ran int8 quantization and saw a 4-6% drop on our chat-turn exact-match eval. Might need per-layer FP16 fallback for output head.

anya: Tried vendorize + auto_map patch. Conversion succeeded after we adjusted tokenizer keys. But generator outputs had misplaced role tokens — chat template still wrong until I normalized the chat templates to use explicit special tokens. Example template we changed: 
```
"chat_template": "<|user|> {user_msg} <|assistant|>"
```
changed to:
```
"chat_template": "{usr_tok} {user_msg} {ass_tok}"
```
and we inject usr_tok/ass_tok from tokenizer.special_tokens_map at conversion time.

sam: Good. Can you paste the minimal loader code you used to verify?

anya: Quick check script that worked: 
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoConfig
config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained('./models/special-chat', trust_remote_code=True)
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('./models/special-chat', use_fast=False)
print(tok.special_tokens_map)
print(tok.additional_special_tokens)
```

priya: Note: using trust_remote_code=True in runtime is OK for internal evals, but for hosted/public models we vendorize and audit classes. Also add a small shim to our converter that normalizes nonstandard keys into the expected mapping. I'll open a PR.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline: conversion-vendorize-job #453 started by anya — logs available at https://ci.redwood.internal/453

anya: Follow-up: conversion+quant pipeline finished. Float32 -> int8 had BLEU-like metric regress of 5% on our dialogue suite. We're running a targeted layer-wise quant sweep next patch. Filing an eval ticket with examples (will attach diffs).

mike: Thanks for the reproducer. Can you add one failing prompt to the eval ticket showing template mismatch? That speeds root-cause.

anya: Yep added 3 examples + diff. PR for tokenizer key-normalization incoming. :thumbsup:
